intro_html: Takeout beef and broccoli, made at home for a fraction of the delivery bill. This skillet stacks 45 grams of protein over rice for about $4.77 a bowl (at everyday cost) and makes 14 servings. Same savory, garlicky, gingery flavor you order out, minus the tip and the wait.
cost_closing_html: About $4.77 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls serves up 45 grams of protein at 596 calories, so it satisfies without weighing you down.
upsell_html: Skip the delivery app this week. You just made it better and cheaper at home. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A bag of frozen broccoli florets costs less than fresh, never wilts in the fridge, and steams in minutes.
The sauce is just soy sauce, broth, and pantry staples, so skip the bottled stir-fry sauces that charge you double for the same thing.
Buy a knob of fresh ginger and a whole garlic bulb once. Pennies per meal and they carry across several recipes in this section.
make_it: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain any excess fat.
Steam or microwave the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender.
Whisk the soy sauce, beef broth, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch into a quick sauce.
Pour the sauce over the beef and simmer until it thickens and glossy-coats the meat.
Fold in the broccoli, then serve everything over cooked rice in each container.

head.description: A high-protein Chinese meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 596 calories and 45 grams of protein for roughly $4.77 each (at everyday cost).
